transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-12-07 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (NexaHealth CTO), Ben Holt (ML Engineer), Rashid Khan (DevOps), Lena Park (Product)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We can do a quick round — I'm Alex, AE, and Priya's our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Sofia: Good, thanks. Running a bit behind this morning but ready.
[00:18] Ben: Hi all, Ben here. Quick note — I have the sample prompt set in the drive, but I need to finalise the labels, will upload by EOD.
[00:28] Priya: Great, that helps. Today I'd like to run through environment readiness — VPC peering, firewall, creds — then quick recap of the small pilot results and next steps for the 50k token benchmark we discussed.
[00:40] Rashid: On VPC peering, we tried peering last week but hit an issue with route tables, so we paused. I'll need exact CIDR ranges and the rules again.
[00:48] Alex: Yep, we'll share the CIDRs and the exact firewall rule set. I'll put that in the onboarding doc this afternoon.
[00:55] Sofia: Also, one of our security folks asked if Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for keys for private deployment.
[01:02] Priya: We do — private deployments can integrate with KMS/HSM. For hosted pilot we can also show envelope encryption and provide SOC 2 docs. We can share the SOC 2 report after an NDA if you want.
[01:15] Sofia: Yes please, send the SOC 2 and any audit log examples.
[01:19] Alex: Noted. We'll attach the compliance packet.

[05:00] Priya: Quick recap on the pilot results — we ran the initial 10k token synthetic load against the small dedicated instance and saw tail latencies around 220-260ms for 512 token calls, throughput around 65 tokens/s in steady state. The KV cache was helping on repeated prefixes but we saw some cold-start spikes.
[05:22] Ben: When you say KV cash — do you mean the key-value cache? We weren't sure if that was enabled on our end; we had some headers turned off.
[05:30] Priya: Yeah, KV cache — sorry bad transcription earlier. We saw about a 15-20% improvement on repeated calls. If you can enable prefix caching on your side it'll help.
[05:40] Ben: Ok, I'll re-check the flags.

[09:00] Alex: On cost side, we reviewed rough numbers last week. For the pilot we're estimating X per-hour for the dedicated GPU node, and you can optimize via quantization and batching. Ben, do you have any hard latency SLOs for the feature?
[09:12] Ben: We want p95 under 500ms for interactive features; for background batch jobs it's less strict. So the 220ms number is fine but we're worried about spikes under load.
[09:24] Priya: For spikes, we recommend two mitigations: 1) small autoscale buffer on dedicated, and 2) fallback model variant in the routing policy to a cheaper smaller model for heavy tails. We can configure that for the canary.
[09:40] Rashid: Autoscale is fine but we need to keep costs predictable; what are the billing implications for autoscale?
[09:48] Alex: Autoscale on Dedicated is usage-based; for pilot we can set a soft cap and Redwood can notify if we hit it. We'll put that in the pilot addendum pricing.

[12:30] Priya: About the 50k token benchmark — plan is: run a 50k token synthetic using your sample prompts, measure throughput, p50/p95/p99, and token cost. We'll run quantized and non-quantized variants and compare.
[12:44] Ben: Sounds good. How long will that take?
[12:47] Priya: The run itself is a few hours including warmup, but we'll need the samples and access set up first. If Rashid can finish VPC peering and open ports today or tomorrow, we can start by Friday.
[12:58] Rashid: I can aim for tomorrow. I need the exact firewall ports — 5100? 5101?
[13:04] Alex: We'll send a checklist with port list and CIDRs. Ports are documented in the onboarding doc; I'll add a one-pager.

[18:00] Sofia: Quick question on data residency — for Private deploy we need all logs to stay in our VPC. Is that supported?
[18:10] Priya: Yes Private (VPC/on-prem) keeps logs in your control, with optional audit log forwarding to your SIEM. Hosted can also provide limited retention and ILM policies but for full control we recommend Private.
[18:24] Sofia: Good, we'll likely push for Private for production but pilot can be hosted or dedicated depending on speed.

[22:00] Ben: Regarding quantization — do you have recommendations? We saw a small accuracy hit at int8 for some prompts.
[22:10] Priya: We generally recommend int8 for throughput-focused endpoints where minor quality delta is acceptable; for critical outputs use 16-bit or a mixed strategy. We'll test both and show quality metrics on the benchmark. We'll also try different prompt truncation and batching policies to reduce cost without impacting quality.
[22:30] Ben: Nice. Could you include example prompts/expected outputs so our product folks can review quality regressions?
[22:36] Alex: Yes — Ben, if you upload the expected outputs we can run automated comparisons and show deltas in the report.

[28:00] Rashid: A quick operational note — our infra team needs the onboarding account to be a service account with stdin keys rotated every 30 days, and SSO delegated to our Okta.
[28:12] Priya: We support Okta SAML SSO and can create service accounts with key rotation policies for Private installs. For hosted pilot we can do time-limited API keys and rotate them per your policy.
[28:24] Rashid: Great. Also need an audit log example for compliance — timestamps, who, action — we want to make sure they meet our retention rules.
[28:32] Alex: We'll include an audit log sample and retention options.

[33:00] Sofia: Anything blocking that would prevent the benchmark this week?
[33:08] Rashid: Just getting the VPC peering and firewall rules applied. If I can get the checklist by EOD I can probably finish tomorrow.
[33:16] Ben: I'm finalising the dataset labels and will upload by EOD too.
[33:22] Alex: Great. So to recap — Redwood will: 1) share onboarding checklist + firewall/CIDR list + SOC2 packet (Alex), 2) SE (Priya) will run and share 50k token benchmark with quantized/non-quantized runs, 3) customer to provide sample prompts/dataset and confirm VPC peering (Ben/Rashid).
[33:40] Priya: We'll also include a suggested routing policy for model fallbacks and an autoscale configuration for the canary.

[38:00] Lena: Product asked if we could see a live demo of canary routing and fallback — maybe a short walkthrough?
[38:10] Priya: We can do a short demo next week, SE-led. I'll show routing table, canary config, and how to promote. Schedule target: early next week — Wednesday or Thursday.
[38:24] Sofia: Wednesday works for us.

[41:00] Alex: Ok final recap and owners — action items in the doc. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the canary demo and share the benchmark spreadsheet when ready. Anything else?
[41:12] Ben: No, thanks.
[41:15] Rashid: Thanks all.
[41:18] Sofia: Thanks, bye.
